title: When Vectors Break Down: Graph-Based RAG for Dense Enterprise Knowledge - Sam Julien, Writer
talk_summary: A Writer DevRel talk describing their multi-year journey from naive vector RAG to graph-based RAG, ending with a knowledge-graph + Fusion-in-Decoder implementation.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of naive fixed-size chunking, they use context-aware splitting and a specialized model to map text into node/edge graph structures, preserving semantic relationships so facts like dates aren't misattributed across chunk boundaries.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we did some uh better contextaware splitting and chunking to uh preserve the context and the semantic relationships

takeaways.technique: Store graph structure as JSON in a Lucene search engine instead of a graph DB
takeaways.what_they_do: They avoided operating a graph database at scale by serializing the graph (nodes/edges) to JSON and indexing it in a Lucene-based search engine, getting relationship-aware retrieval without graph-DB operational cost.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we stored the data points as JSON in a lucine based search engine

takeaways.technique: Benchmark retrieval against multiple baselines on a public QA set
takeaways.what_they_do: They benchmarked their retrieval system against seven vector-search systems on Amazon's RobustQA dataset, reporting best accuracy and fastest response time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: compared our retrieval system with knowledge graph and fusion decoder and everything uh with our with seven different vector search uh systems
takeaways.numbers: 7 vector-search baselines compared; claimed best accuracy and fastest response time

takeaways.technique: Solve the problem, not the hyped solution
takeaways.what_they_do: The team repeatedly stepped back from whatever technique was trendy and re-derived the approach from the actual customer problem and their own team's strengths.
takeaways.evidence_quote: solving the customer problems rather than implementing specific solutions

takeaways.technique: Use small CPU/small-GPU specialized models for structured transforms
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than paying for large models or graph DBs, they fine-tuned a small model that runs on CPUs/smaller GPUs to convert text into graph structures.
takeaways.evidence_quote: let's build a specialized model that can scale and run on CPUs or smaller GPUs
